newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada daily lumber export figures to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canada daily lumber export figures to U.S..

text.p: Canada softwood lumber exports to the United States as of 0001 EST on March 10 in board feet, according to data from the Canadian Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade:
For the Jan 1 - March 31 quarter:
Province BC Alberta Ontario Quebec Total
bonus 12.44 million 9.98 million 9.14 million 44.50 million 76.06 mln
EB 1.21 bln 144.38 million 193.33 million 356.38 million 1.91 bln
LFB 71.63 million 10.86 million 24.24 million 40.95 million 147.69 mln
UFB 30.64 million 8.04 million 37.96 million 83.68 million 160.33 mln
Pct exported: EB - 12.96, LFB - 22.72
For the Oct 1 - Dec 31 quarter:
Province BC Alberta Ontario Quebec Total
bonus 6.36 million 7.66 million 9.33 million 51.06 million 74.41 mln
EB 2.12 bln 293.38 million 412.15 million 892.66 million 3.72 bln
LFB 3.80 million 10.57 million 6.39 million 12.03 million 32.80 mln
UFB 6.71 million 12.32 million 4.55 million 28.29 million 51.86 mln
Pct exported: EB - 25.29, LFB - 5.04
April 1 - present:
Province BC Alberta Ontario Quebec Total
bonus 18.80 million 17.64 million 18.46 million 95.56 million 150.47 mln
EB 7.97 bln 1.08 bln 1.56 bln 3.36 bln 13.96 bln
LFB 138.03 million 26.19 million 59.22 million 130.63 million 354.07 mln
UFB 37.35 million 20.36 million 42.51 million 111.97 million 212.19 mln
Pct exported: EB - 94.96, LFB - 54.47.
Source: Export and Import Controls Bureau, Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade.
NOTE: EB = established base shipments, LFB = lower fee base, UFB = upper base fee.

From April 1, Canadian lumber exports which exceed quarterly or annual quotas are subject to export fees. Exports above 14.7 billion board feet annually or 4.226 billion board feet quarterly are subject to US$50 fee for every 1,000 board feet. If such excess exports exceed 650 million board feet, they are subject to a US$100 fee for every 1,000 board feet.
Export quotas are allocated for each province on a company-by-company basis. Shippers who have not been given an allocation are subject to the US$100 fee for any lumber they export.
This export data is based on Canadian export permits. There is a one-week lag between the entry of softwood lumber into the United States and the application for a Canadian permit.
